playoff.note: 11th plays the Qatar Stars League 2 runner-up in a single match for the last top-flight place; 12th is relegated directly

format.note: eight clubs, 14 rounds derived from a double round-robin; no 2026-27 season article exists to quote a round count

playoff.note: champion promoted directly; runner-up meets the QSL 11th in a single match

boundaries.note: QSL2 champion goes up directly, runner-up plays the QSL 11th in a single match; QSL 12th goes down directly and 11th risks the same play-off, so exactly one of {QSL 11th, QSL2 runner-up} is in the top flight next season.

conflicts.note: Confirmed by the English 2026-27 club list and by the Spanish and Arabic league articles, both of which say eight. Our 12 looks like a copy of the QSL figure.

conflicts.real: the English article says the champion plays the 10th-placed QSL club and the runner-up is not mentioned
conflicts.note: Outdated 2022-23 rule. The 2026-27 QSL table marks 11th as the play-off place and the Arabic article describes runner-up v second-last. Current shape used.

conflicts.ours: no relegation from the second tier
conflicts.real: the English infobox lists relegation to a 'Qatar Stars League 3', while its own body text and the Spanish/Arabic articles say there is no relegation and no third tier

notes: QSL: 12 clubs, 22 rounds, champion on points, 12th relegated and 11th in a single-match play-off against the QSL2 runner-up. QSL2: 8 clubs, not 12; 14 rounds is arithmetic because no 2026-27 season article exists. The second tier's 2026-27 field includes Al Rayyan Next-Gen, a reserve side formed in 2026. Sources disagree on whether QSL2 relegates (English infobox mentions a QSL3 that no other source supports) and on which QSL place enters the play-off (10th in the outdated English text, 11th in the 2026-27 tables and the Arabic article). Both levels use plain double round-robins with no split.
